about.title: Maricopa Slip & Fall & Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Maricopa is a small community along Rt 166 and California Street, home to gas stations, small shops, and roadside businesses that see steady traffic from travelers and locals alike. When a property owner lets a spill, broken step, or icy walkway go unaddressed, the person who falls often ends up carrying the cost. California law requires an injured person to show the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn visitors. In a town this size, evidence can disappear fast — spills get mopped up, surveillance footage gets overwritten, and witnesses move on. Acting early to document what happened, photograph the scene, and request that any video be preserved can matter a great deal. We handle premises liability claims and can evaluate your fall and explain your options under California's two-year filing deadline.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Maricopa Premises Case

items.title: Proving the Owner Had Notice
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't act. We can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records to build that case.

items.title: Preserving Surveillance Footage Fast
items.desc: Small businesses along California Street or Rt 166 may overwrite security video within days. Sending a preservation request quickly can be the difference between having evidence and having none.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover even if you were partly responsible for the fall, though your share reduces the total. We can help present the facts in a way that protects your share of the claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Maricopa?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a government building, the deadline is much shorter and requires a separate claims process. It's best to get a case reviewed early so no deadline is missed.

items.question: What if the store or property owner says I was partly at fault?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so being partially responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation — it just reduces the amount based on your share of fault. We can help gather evidence that shows what really happened. Don't assume a partial-fault claim isn't worth pursuing.

items.question: There aren't many businesses in Maricopa — does that affect my case?
items.answer: A smaller town doesn't change California premises liability law, but it can affect how quickly evidence disappears since local businesses may not routinely preserve footage or records. Acting quickly to document the hazard and request video retention is especially important here. Our team is familiar with rural Kern County claims and can guide you through those early steps.

items.question: Do I have to pay anything to get a case review?
items.answer: No. Our case review is free, and we generally work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost to have your case reviewed.
